nodes.title: PRELIMINARY
nodes.body: The regulations contained in Table C (as prescribed by Section 8 of The Companies Act 1985) in force at the date of adoption of these Articles shall not apply to the Company.

In these regulations:-

“Act” means The Companies Act 1985 to 2006 (including any statutory modification or re-enactment thereof for the time being in force);

“Articles” means the Articles of Association of the Company;

“Board of Directors” the members of the Board of Directors for the time being elected at the Annual General Meeting or co-opted pursuant to Article 18.8, any other Directors elected from time to time at any General Meeting of the Company to fill any vacancies and the Chairman of the Company from time to time”;

“CEO” means Chief Executive Officer (if any);

“Chairman” means the Chairman of the Board as appointed pursuant to Article 14.2.

“Chairman of a meeting” shall mean the Chairman or such person who shall chair of a meeting of the Company or of the Company’s Board from time to time.

“Clear Days” means in relation to the period of a notice that period excluding the day when the notice is given or deemed to be given and the day for which it is given or on which it is to take effect;

“Club” means any football club which is for the time being admitted to the Competition under the Rules;

“Commercial Agreements” means any agreement entered into by the Competition for the Competition with a third party for the purpose of generating income or goodwill to the Company or Competition for the provision of services to the Company or Competition.

“Company” means The Football Conference Limited;

“Company Secretary” means Secretary of the Company, from time to time, in accordance with Company Law;

“Competition” means the football competition to be managed by the Company under the name of “The Football Conference” (or such other name as the Company may adopt thereafter) and consisting of the football clubs who are from time to time members of the Company;

“Football Creditors” means those persons in respect of whose debts the Board of Directives has power to impose penalties on Members Clubs under Article 5.3.5 being:
The Football Association Limited
Any Club affiliated with an Affiliated Association
Any League sanctioned by The Association or an Affiliated Association

Any full time or part time employee of a Club, or former full time or part time employee of a Club, in respect of sums due to such person by way of arrears of remuneration or expenses. This excludes for these purposes all and any claims for redundancy, unfair or wrongful dismissal or other claims arising out of the termination of the contract or in respect of any period after the actual date of termination
The Professional Footballers’ Association Limited
The Football Foundation
Any Affiliated Association

Any pension scheme or plan administered by or on behalf of the Competition

“GM” means any person appointed to the role of General Manager of the Company, and if there is no person appointed, the CEO;

"Independent" means a person who shall not be a Director or Officer of any member Club of the Competition.

"National League" means the National first tier of the Competition, notwithstanding that it may be designated as a different title from time to time.

"National League North" means the Northern secondary tier of the Competition, notwithstanding that it may be designated as a different title from time to time.

"National League South" means the Southern secondary tier of the Competition, notwithstanding that it may be designated as a different title from time to time.

“Office” means the registered office of the Company;

“Officers of the Competition” means the CEO, the GM and the Company Secretary or such of those positions as may be filled from time to time.

“Qualifying Director” A Director shall qualify to be one of the Directors provided he is a Director of a Club which shall be playing in the Competition.

“Rules” means the Standardised Rules of the Competition issued by the Football Association (subject to such amendments as shall from time to time be made or adopted by the Company);

“Step 1 Club” means any Club in the National League for the time being.

“Step 2 Club” means any Club in the National League North or National League South for the time being.

“the United Kingdom” means Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

“Vice Chairman” means Vice Chairman of the Board as appointed pursuant to Article 14.3.

Unless the context otherwise requires, words or expressions contained in these regulations bear the same meaning as in the Act but excluding any statutory modifications thereof not in force when these regulations become binding on the Company.
A reference to a person includes a body corporate and an unincorporated body of persons.
The number of members with which the Company proposes to be registered is up to 72.
The provisions of section 352 of the Act shall be observed by the Company.

Every Club which is a corporation or body corporate and which signs and submits a membership application form (in the form detailed in Article 4 hereof ) shall be deemed to become a member on its name being entered in the register of members together with the particulars required by Section 352 of the Act.

Every Club which is an unincorporated association shall be obliged to nominate an individual as its nominee. Each nominee shall act in all respects in accordance with the directions of the Club which has appointed him.

Every Club which is an unincorporated association shall be entitled to submit a membership application form (in the form detailed in Article 4 hereof) with such modifications as the Board of Directors shall require. The appointed nominee shall be deemed to become a member on his name being entered in the register of members.

Every Club which is an unincorporated association shall be entitled at any time and from time to time upon notice in writing to the Company to require the deletion of the name of its appointed nominee for the time being and the substitution thereof of the name of another nominee to act on its behalf. Any such alteration in the name of the appointed nominee shall not affect the rights, privileges and obligations of any such Club in relation to membership of the Company.

Members shall be only such Clubs, or in the case of unincorporated associations the duly appointed nominees of such Clubs, which are in membership of the Competition for the time being in accordance with the Rules. Without prejudice to Article 3.4, the names of the clubs in the Competition will be determined by the Board of Directors and ratified at the Annual General Meeting.

Any Club, or in the case of an unincorporated Association the duly appointed nominee of any Club, which is a member of the Company by virtue of the Club in question being in membership of the Competition shall automatically cease to be a member of the Company on the Club in question ceasing to be in membership of the Competition and in such circumstances the name of such Club (in the case of a corporation or body corporate) or the name of such Club’s duly appointed nominee (in the case of an unincorporated association) shall be removed from the register of members forthwith.

Every Club shall deliver to the Company an application for membership of the Company in the following form, or in such form as the Board of Directors may require, which shall be signed (in the case of a Club) for and on behalf of the Club by two of its directors (in the case of companies) or officers (in the case of unincorporated associations).

THE FOOTBALL CONFERENCE LIMITED

*I (name)………………………………………of (address).…………………………………………………………………….

*We (name)…………………………………..of (address)……………………………............…….………*Director/Officer

and (name)……………………………………of (address)……………………………………............…....*Director/Officer

and (name)……………………………………of (address)……………………………………..……….....…………………..

and (name)……………………………………of (address)…………………………………..…………….....………………..

being *directors/officers of…......................................................................................……….Football Club (“the Club”)

having been provided with a copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association of The Football Conference Limited (“the Company”) and a copy of its rules, do hereby [confirm that we are authorised on behalf of the Club to sign this application and] agree [on behalf of the Club], that if the Club [or its duly appointed nominee] is/I am accepted into membership of the Company, to comply with and be bound by the Memorandum and Articles of Association and rules of the Company and to procure our duly appointed nominee to so conform to and be bound by the Memorandum, Articles and Rules and to accept, abide by and implement the decisions of the Board of Directors of the Company* [and to procure our duly appointed nominee to so accept, abide by and implement such decisions]. *[If this application for membership is accepted we, on behalf of the Club, hereby nominate [] as nominee of the Club, and understand and accept that since the Club is an unincorporated association the nominee’s name will be entered in the register of members together with such other particulars as shall be required. In the event that such individual wishes to resign as the Club’s nominee or in the event that the Club wishes to remove such individual as its nominee we, on behalf of the Club, undertake to nominate a person forthwith as a replacement therefore in accordance with Article 3.2.4 whose name shall be entered in the register of members as the Club’s nominee in place of the person so resigning or so removed.]

Date

(*Delete as applicable)
The membership application form when completed and signed shall be deposited with the secretary of the Company at the office.

nodes.title: RESIGNATION AND REMOVAL OF A MEMBER

nodes.body: Any Club may resign from membership of the Company at the end of a playing season of the Competition and prior to the annual general meeting following the end of such playing season provided it has notified the CEO and /or the GM as appropriate of its decision to so resign on or before 31 January in that season.

A member may be expelled by the unanimous decision of those present and eligible to vote at a quorate meeting of the Board of Directors. In the event of there simply being a majority decision then the Board of Directors shall within a minimum of seven (7) days convene a meeting of the Clubs from the Division in which the Club the subject of the decision shall be playing. Pending such a meeting the Board of Directors may suspend the relevant member Club from the Competition. In the event of the Clubs voting in favour of the expulsion by a vote of at least 75% of those present either in person or by written proxy then the Board of Directors shall forthwith expel the relevant Club. The Club the subject of the vote shall not be entitled to vote but shall be entitled to be present at the meeting and to present a statement in defence of its position and in opposition to the expulsion either verbally or in writing. In the event of the expulsion being during the Playing Season then all of the expelled Club’s playing record shall be expunged and the expelled member Club shall be erased from the Competition’s register of members.
A member must inform the General Manager immediately if that member:
has a manager, receiver or administrative receiver appointed in respect of it or any part of its undertaking or assets;
has a petition presented for an administrative order or if an administration order shall be made in respect of it;
has a winding up order made in respect of it;

passes a resolution for its winding up or enters into any arrangement with its creditors or some part of them in respect of a payment of its debts or part of them as a creditors voluntary arrangement under the Insolvency Act 1986: and in such circumstances, the Directors may expel the member from the competition forthwith or may give notice to the member that it shall be expelled from a certain date (“Notice of Expulsion”). Where the Directors give “Notice of Expulsion”, the Directors may impose such conditions on the member concerned for the intervening period as they see fit and may amend and withdraw such conditions or impose new conditions at any time.

Where a Member Club (defaulting Club) defaults in making any payments to any Football Creditor the “Defaulting Club” shall be subject to such penalty as the Board of Directors may decide in addition to any Sporting Sanctions penalties to be imposed under the Rules.
All meetings of the Members other than annual general meetings shall be called general meetings.

The Board of Directors may call general meetings and, on the requisition of members pursuant to the provisions of the Act, shall forthwith proceed to convene a general meeting for a date not later than forty days after the receipt of the requisition. If there is not a quorum of the Board members within the United Kingdom to enable a meeting of the Board of Directors to be held and a resolution to be passed thereat to call a general meeting, any Board Member or any Member may call a general meeting.

If the Board of Directors considers any resolution(s) proposed to be voted upon at any general meeting convened in accordance with these Articles is only applicable to Step 1 Clubs, the Board of Directors shall determine (and if so shall specify in the notice convening the general meeting) that only Members representing Step 1 Clubs may vote on such Resolution(s).

If the Board of Directors considers any resolution(s) proposed to be voted upon at any general meeting convened in accordance with these Articles is only applicable to Step 2 Clubs, the Board of Directors shall determine (and if so shall specify in the notice convening the general meeting) that only Members representing Step 2 Clubs may vote on such Resolution(s).
An annual general meeting and any general meeting shall be called by at least fourteen (14) Clear Days’ notice. Meetings may be called by shorter notice if it is so agreed:
in the case of an annual general meeting, by all the members entitled to attend and vote thereat; and

in the case of any other meeting, by a majority in number of the members having a right to attend and vote being a majority together holding not less than ninety-five per cent of the total voting rights at the meeting of all the members.

The notice shall specify the time and place of the meeting and the general nature of the business to be transacted and, in the case of an annual general meeting, shall specify the meeting as such. Subject to the provisions of the Articles, the notice shall be given to all members, the Board of Directors, the auditors and to any life members (provided that there shall be no obligation to give any notice to a Club which is an unincorporated association when notice has been given to its duly appointed nominee).
The accidental omission to give notice of a meeting to, or the non-receipt of notice of a meeting by, any person entitled to receive notice shall not invalidate the processing at that meeting.

The annual general meeting shall be held on the second Saturday in June each year unless otherwise decided by the Board of Directors (provided that no more than fifteen months shall elapse between annual general meetings).
The following business shall be transacted at the annual general meeting:
the minutes of the preceding annual general meeting, having been circulated, will be confirmed and business arising therefrom dealt with;
the adoption of standing orders;
The presentation and adoption of the annual report;
the election of members of the Board of Directors and auditors;
The Constitution of membership of The Competition for the following season:
any alteration to the Articles and Rules; and

the consideration of any other business (of which, subject to Article 7.1.1, at least fourteen Clear Days’

notice must have been given).

A copy of the audited accounts of the Company approved at a special meeting of the Company held in the preceding January and the agenda for that meeting shall be sent to each Member with notice of the annual general meeting. Annual accounts will be distributed for approval at a special meeting of all members in January each year following the annual general meeting. Notice of such a special meeting will be provided in accordance with Article 8.1 and 8.2. The Company’s accounting year shall be from 1st July to 30th June each year.

No business shall be transacted at any general meeting (including the annual general meeting) unless a quorum is present. Not less than three-fifths of members for the time being entitled to vote upon the business to be transacted each (subject to the proviso contained at article 3.3) being a duly appointed nominee of a Club which is an unincorporated association or present by a duly authorised representative in the case of a Club which is a corporation or body corporate shall be a quorum.

If such a quorum is not present within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting, or if during a meeting such a quorum ceases to be present, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place or to such time and place as the Board of Directors may determine.

The Chairman or, failing him, some other Board Member nominated by the Board of Directors shall preside as chairman of the meeting, but if neither the Chairman nor such other Board Member (if any) be present within fifteen minutes after the time appointed for holding the meeting and willing to act, the Board Members present shall elect one of their number to be chairman and, if there is only one such Board Member present and willing to act, he shall be Chairman.

If no Board Member is willing to act as Chairman, or if no such Board Member is present within fifteen minutes after the time appointed for holding the meeting, the members of the Board present and entitled to vote shall choose one of their number to be Chairman.

The Chairman may, with the consent of a meeting at which a quorum is present (and shall if so directed by resolution of the meeting), adjourn the meeting from time to time and from place to place, but no business shall be transacted at an adjourned meeting other than business which might properly have been transacted at the meeting had the adjournment not taken place.

When a meeting is adjourned for fourteen days or more, at least seven clear days’ notice shall be given specifying the time and place of the adjourned meeting and the general nature of the business to be transacted. Otherwise it shall not be necessary to give any such notice.

nodes.title: VOTING AT GENERAL MEETINGS (TO INCLUDE THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING AND ANY EXTRA-ORDINARY MEETING)

nodes.body: Subject to Articles 12.2 and 12.3 at any General Meeting (including the Annual General Meeting) each Member being a member Club shall have one vote.

If in the notice convening a general meeting it is specified that only Members representing Step 1 Clubs may vote on a Resolution(s), each Member being a Step 1 Club shall have one vote on that Resolution (and no member Club in Step 2 shall be entitled to vote on it) and

If in the notice convening a general meeting it is specified that only Members representing Step 2 Clubs may vote on a Resolution(s), each Member being a Step 2 Club shall have one vote on that Resolution (and no member Club in Step 1 shall be entitled to vote on it).

Subject as otherwise provided in these regulations, a resolution put to the vote of a meeting shall be decided on a show of hands unless before, or on the declaration of the result of the show of hands, a poll is duly demanded. Subject to the provisions of the Act, a poll may be demanded:
by the Chairman; or
by at least four members having the right to vote at the meeting; (and a demand by a person as proxy for a member shall be the same as a demand by the member).

A poll shall be taken as the Chairman directs and he may appoint scrutinisers (who need not be members) and fix a time and a place for declaring the result of the poll. The result of the poll shall be deemed to be the resolution of the meeting at which the poll was demanded.

Subject as otherwise provided in these regulations, on a show of hands every member who (being an unincorporated association) is entitled to be present by its nominee or (being a company or body corporate) is present by its duly authorised representative shall have one vote and on a poll every member so present by representative or nominee or present by proxy shall have one vote.
Where all Members are entitled to vote on a proposed resolution of the Company, such resolution shall be deemed passed if:
a majority of votes of Members who are Step 1 Clubs are in favour of such resolution; and
a majority of votes of all Members are in favour of such resolution.

If in the notice convening a general meeting it is specified that only Members representing Step 1 Clubs or only Members representing Step 2 Clubs may vote on a Resolution, such resolution shall be deemed passed if a majority of Step 1 Clubs or a majority of Step 2 Clubs (as the case may be) votes in favour of such resolution.

Any company or body corporate which is a member may by resolution of its directors or other governing body authorise such person (who shall be a member of the Board of Directors or Board of Directors of that Club) as it thinks fit to act as its representative at any meeting of the Company, and the person so authorised shall be entitled to exercise the same powers on behalf of the Company or body corporate which he represents as that Club could (to the extent that it is otherwise entitled to do so) exercise if it were an individual member of the Company.

Each member club shall ensure that its representative or nominee attends each General Meeting of the Company. save where attendance at a General Meeting is limited to a particular Step, in which case only those representatives or nominees of member Clubs in the particular Step in question need attend. The representative or nominee must be a member of the Board of Directors of that Club or an Officer of that Club. Any Club failing to be represented at any General Meeting (or applicable meeting of a particular Step) of the Company will pay a fine of £250 to the Company. Each member may in addition to its duly authorised representative or it’s duly appointed nominee, have in attendance at those General Meetings is entitled to attend as an observer who shall take no part in the proceedings.

Subject to Article 12.12, evidence to the satisfaction of the Board Members of the authority of the person claiming to exercise the right to vote at any meeting of the Company shall be deposited at the Office not less than 48 hours before the time appointed for holding the meeting or adjourned meeting at which the right to vote is being exercised and in default the right to vote shall not be exercisable by that person.
On a poll a vote may be given either personally or by proxy.

An instrument appointing a proxy shall be in writing, executed by or on behalf of the appointer and shall be in the following form (or in a form as near thereto as circumstances allow or in any other form which the Board Members may approve):

THE FOOTBALL CONFERENCE LIMITED

I/We, …………………..……..of …………....................………………… being a member/members of the above-named company, hereby appoint……………….of.. ………………………....................…… or failing him/her , ..……………..of ………....…………… as my/our proxy to vote in my/our name(s) and on my/our behalf at the annual/ general meeting of the Company to be held on ……………………....................…………………. and at any adjournment thereof.

This form is to be used in respect of the resolutions mentioned below as follows:

Resolution No 1 *for* against Resolution No 2 *for* against *Strike out whichever is not desired. Unless otherwise instructed, the proxy may vote as he thinks fit or abstain from voting.

Signed: …………….............……………… Dated:………………………

The instrument appointing a proxy and any authority under which it is executed shall be deposited at the office or at such other place within the United Kingdom as is specified in the notice convening the meeting or in any instrument of proxy sent out by the Company in relation to the meeting not less than 48 hours before the time appointed for holding the meeting or adjourned meeting at which the person named in the instrument proposes to vote.

If a poll is not taken forthwith but is taken not more than 48 hours after it was demanded the instrument appointing a proxy and any authority under which it is executed may be delivered at the meeting at which the poll was demanded to the Chairman or to the CEO or to any Board Member.

Only a member who shall have paid every subscription and other sum (if any), which shall be due and payable to the Company in respect of its membership pursuant to the Rules or otherwise, shall (to the extent that it is otherwise entitled to do so) be entitled to be present or represented or to vote on any question at any general meeting of the Company.
In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall be entitled to a second or casting vote in addition to any other vote he may have.

A declaration by the Chairman that a resolution has been carried or carried unanimously, or by a particular majority, or lost, or not carried by a particular majority and an entry to that effect in the minutes of the meeting shall be conclusive evidence of the fact without proof of the number or proportion of the votes recorded in favour of or against the resolution.
A Board Member shall, notwithstanding that he is not a member, be entitled to attend and speak at any general meeting.

No objection shall be raised as to the qualification of any voter except at the meeting or adjourned meeting at which the vote objected to be tendered, and every vote not disallowed at the meeting shall be valid. Any objection may in due time be referred to the Chairman whose decision shall be final and conclusive.

nodes.title: RESOLUTIONS OF THE MEMBERS IN WRITING
nodes.body: A resolution in writing executed by or on behalf of each member who would have been entitled to vote upon it if it had been proposed at a general meeting at which he was present in person or by a duly authorised representative shall be as effectual as if it had been passed at a general meeting duly convened and held and may consist of several instruments in the like form each executed by or on behalf of one or more members.

Unless otherwise determined by special resolution, the number of Board Members shall be 13 consisting of 6 Board Members who shall be required to be Directors of a National League Club, 2 Board Members who shall be required to be Directors of a National League North Club, 2 Board Members who shall be required to be Directors of a National League South Club, 2 persons who are not Directors or Officers of any member Club of the Competition (“Independent Board Members”) and the Chairman. A member of the Management Committee of an unincorporated member of the Competition shall be regarded as a Director of a Club for the purpose of this Article only.

The Board of Directors shall appoint the Chairman and the Independent Board Members. Each of the Chairman and each Independent Board Member shall be an independent person who shall not be a Director or Officer of any member Club of the Competition. The Chairman shall not be a Director of the Company and shall not be entitled to vote at Board meetings save by way of a casting vote in his capacity of Chairman of a Board meeting. The Independent Board Members shall be Directors of the Company and shall be entitled to vote at Board meetings. In his absence, the acting Chairman of a Board meeting shall have a casting vote even if he shall have already voted as a Director. The Chairman and each of the Independent Board Members shall be appointed for an initial period of 1 year and any reappointment by the Board shall be for a further period of 2 years. In the event of any Chairman or Independent Board Member intending to resign at the end of his period of tenure or not wishing to seek reappointment, he shall be obliged to advise the Competition in writing by 1 January preceding the expiry of his term. In the event of any Chairman or Independent Board Member wishing to resign mid-term then he shall be obliged to advise the Competition in writing by 1 January preceding the next following AGM.

A Vice-Chairman shall be appointed at the first meeting of the Board following the AGM in any year. There shall be no requirement for the Vice-Chairman to be selected from the Board Members who are eligible to vote at Board meetings. Where the Vice-Chairman is selected from the Board Members who are eligible to vote, he shall not be entitled to an additional vote at Board meetings save where, in the absence of the Chairman, he shall be acting as Chairman of any Board meeting when he shall be entitled to have a casting vote as Chairman of the meeting.
Any number of non-voting Board members may be co-opted.

Subject to the provisions of the Act, the Memorandum of Association and the Articles, the business of the Company shall be managed by the Board of Directors who may exercise all the powers of the Company and shall enforce the Rules. The Board of Directors shall meet as often as is necessary to transact the business of the Company and shall except as expressly provided herein, have jurisdiction over all matters affecting the Company including any not provided for in the Rules. No alteration of the Memorandum of Association, the Articles or the Rules shall invalidate any prior act of the Board of Directors which would have been valid if that alteration had not been made. The powers given by this regulation shall not be limited by any special power given to the Board of Directors by the Articles and a meeting of the Board of Directors at which a quorum is present may exercise all powers exercisable by the Board of Directors.
The Board of Directors shall make and issue decisions in accordance with the Rules as such Rules may be amended or replaced in accordance with Article 25.

The Board of Directors may, by power of attorney or otherwise, appoint any person to be the agent of the Company for such purposes and on such conditions as it determines, including authority for the agent to delegate all or any of his powers.

nodes.title: DELEGATION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS’S POWERS

nodes.body: The Board of Directors may appoint Sub-Committees and may delegate any of its powers to any Sub-Committee as it may deem necessary. The Board of Directors may also delegate such powers to the CEO or any other officer.

Any such delegation may be made subject to any conditions the Board of Directors may impose and either collaterally with or to the exclusion of the powers of the Board of Directors and may be revoked or altered at any time.
Subject to any such conditions, the proceedings of a Sub-Committee shall be governed by the Articles regulating the proceedings of the Board of Directors so far as they are capable of applying.
The decisions or recommendations of all such Sub-Committees shall be reported to the Board of Directors.
A member of a sub-Committee need not be a member of the Board or an Officer of the Competition.
The Officers of the Competition shall be removed and appointed from time to time by the Board of Directors.
Each person while he is an Officer of the Competition shall not be a member of the Board of Directors but shall be entitled to attend Board meetings.

nodes.title: APPOINTMENT AND RETIREMENT OF BOARD MEMBERS

nodes.body: No person who is not a Director, an Independent Board Member or a Member of a Board of Directors of a Club in membership of the Competition or a Member of the Management Committee of an unincorporated member of the Competition shall be eligible to hold office as a Board Member and be entitled to vote.

Subject to clause 14.2, a Director shall be entitled to serve a term of office for a period of 3 years from the date of his or her election or until the third General Meeting after the General Meeting at which he or she was elected whichever is the earlier. A Director shall be entitled to seek re-election after the expiry of his or her initial 3 year term for a further period of 3 years and at the expiry of each 3 year term may seek re-election for a further period of 3 years. A Board Member shall cease to be eligible to be a Director on the Board at the first Annual General Meeting after the Board Member’s 75th birthday and no nomination will be eligible after the nominee’s 75th birthday.

A Director of a Club which is no longer in the section of the Competition he/she represents shall be obliged to retire but may offer him/herself up for re-election for a Board position representing the Division of the Competition in which his club will be playing in the following season.

Subject as hereinafter provided, no person shall be elected or re-elected a Director at any AGM unless he is proposed by a member and seconded by another member by notice in writing to the GM by no later than 14 clear days before the AGM following the nomination (“the Closing Date”). Any individual accepting a nomination shall be obliged to lodge his full CV with the Company’s GM no later than seven clear days before the AGM and failing that his nomination shall be null and void.

In the event of there being insufficient nominations by the Closing Date then nominations may continue to be made until noon on the day of the Annual General Meeting. All additional nominees (even if they are existing Board members) shall still be obliged to provide a CV unless their nomination is made and accepted less than 7 days before the AGM.
All of the above shall be applied on a division by division and region by region basis.

In the event of any Director being a Director representing the National League, the National League North or the National League South and the Club of which he is a Director moving from one Division to the other then he shall only be eligible to stand as a Director representing the Division in which his Club is a member at the date of the relevant General Meeting at which he is seeking re-election and if his Club is relegated during his term of office then he shall be obliged to resign at the AGM at which such relegation is confirmed.

Not less than 14 clear days prior to the date appointed for holding the AGM notice shall be given to all who

are entitled to receive notice of the meeting of any person who is recommended for election or re-election as a

Board Member at the meeting or in respect of whom Notice has been duly given to the Company of the intention to

propose him at the meeting for election or re-election as a Board Member/Director. In the event of there

being insufficient nominations by that date and further nominations being received in accordance with Article 18.5

then notice shall be given of such nominations to all who are entitled to receive notice as above as soon as such

nominations are received.

The Board of Directors may appoint a qualifying person who is willing to act as a Board member to fill a

vacancy and the Board member so appointed shall hold office only until the AGM following his appointment when

he shall be obliged to resign albeit with the right to stand for re-election. Such Board Member during his period of

membership shall be entitled to vote.

The Board of Directors may at any time co-opt a non-executive Director (who shall not be required to be a director of a member club of the Competition) on to the Board and who shall be entitled to attend all Board meetings but who shall not be entitled to vote at the same. The Board of Directors may also at any time co-opt a Director of a Competition member on to the Board. However, he shall only be entitled to vote if his appointment is pursuant to Article 18.9 hereof. Details of such co-opted Director or Directors shall be provided to all Clubs within 28 days of such appointment.
No Club shall have more than one of its representatives with voting powers on the Board of Directors.

nodes.title: DISQUALIFICATION AND REMOVAL OF BOARD MEMBERS

nodes.body: The office of a Board Member shall (if a Board Member appointed in accordance with Article 18) be vacated if:
he ceases to be a Board Member by virtue of any provision of the Act or he becomes prohibited by law from being a Board Member; or
he becomes bankrupt or makes any arrangement or composition with his creditors generally; or
he is, or maybe, suffering from mental disorder and either:

he is admitted to hospital in pursuance of an application for admission for treatment under The Mental

Health Act 1983 or, in Scotland, an application for admission under The Mental Health (Scotland) Act 1960, or

an order is made by a court having jurisdiction (whether in the United Kingdom or elsewhere) in matters concerning mental disorder for his detention or for the appointment of a receiver, curator bonis or other person to exercise powers with respect to his property or affairs; or
he resigns his office by notice to the Company; or

he shall for more than three consecutive months have been absent without permission of the Board of Directors from meetings of the Board of Directors held during that period or he shall have been absent without permission from more than one half of the meetings of the Board of Directors in any period of one year and (in either case) the Board of Directors resolves that his office be vacated; or

(if a Board Member appointed in accordance with Article 18) he ceases to be a director of or a member of the Board of Directors of a Club in membership of the Competition or the Club in question or, in the case of an unincorporated association, the duly appointed nominee of such Club ceases to be a member of that Club; or
he is removed from office under section 303 of the Act; or
if a Board Member only by virtue of being an Officer of the Competition, he ceases to be an Officer of the Competition; or
the other members of the Board of Directors unanimously resolve that his office be vacated.

nodes.title: EXPENSES
nodes.body: A Board Member may be paid all reasonable expenses properly incurred by him in connection with the discharge of their duties.

Subject to the provisions of the Act and to the Memorandum of Association, the Board of Directors may appoint one or more of its number to any executive office and may enter into an agreement or arrangement with any Board Member for his employment by the Company. Any such appointment, agreement or arrangement may be made upon such terms as the Board of Directors determine and they may remunerate any such Board Member for his services as they think fit. Any appointment of a Board Member to an executive office shall, unless otherwise determined by the Company in general meeting, terminate if he ceases to be a Board Member but without general prejudice to any claim to damages for breach of the contract of service between the Board Member and the Company.

Subject to Article 23.1 and to the provisions of the Act and to the Memorandum of Association and provided that he has disclosed to the Board of Directors the nature and extent of any material interest of his, a Board Member notwithstanding his office:
may be a party to, or otherwise interested in, any transaction or arrangement with the Company or in which the Company is otherwise interested;

may be a director or other officer of, or employed by, or a party to any transaction or arrangement with, or otherwise interested in, any body corporate promoted by the Company or in which the Company is otherwise or interested; and

shall not, by reason of his office, be accountable to the Company for any benefit which he derives from any such office or employment or from any such transaction or arrangement or from any interest in any such body corporate and no such transaction or arrangement shall be liable to be avoided on the ground of any such interest or benefit.

For the purposes of Article 21.2:

a general notice given to the Board of Directors that a Board Member is to be regarded as having interest of the nature and extent specified in the notice in any transaction or arrangement in which a specified person or class of persons is interested shall be deemed to be a disclosure that the Board Member has an interest in any such transaction of the nature and extent so specified; and
all interest of which a Board Member has no knowledge and of which it is unreasonable to expect him to have knowledge shall not be treated as an interest of his.

Subject to the provisions of the Articles the Board members may regulate their proceedings as they think fit. A Board member may, and the CEO and/or the General Manager shall at the request of a Board member call a meeting of the Board of Directors. Questions arising at such a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes. Subject to the provisions of these Articles, each Board member shall have one vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have the second or casting vote.

The quorum for the transaction of the business of the Board of Directors shall be four (4) but no vote shall be taken unless there shall be not less than three (3) members present representing Conference Premier Clubs and one member representing either Conference North or Conference South.

The continuing Board Members or a sole continuing Board Member may act notwithstanding any vacancies in their number, but, if the number of Board Members is less than the number fixed as the quorum, the continuing Board of Directors or Board Member may act only for the purposes of filling vacancies or of calling a general meeting.

Unless he is unwilling to do so, the Chairman shall preside at every meeting of the Board of Directors at which he is present. But, if there is no person holding either office, or if the person holding it is unwilling to preside or is not present within five minutes after the time appointed for the meeting, the Board Members present may appoint one of their number to be chairman of the meeting.

All acts done by a meeting of the Board of Directors, or of a Board of the Board of Directors, or by a person acting as a Board Member shall, notwithstanding that it be afterwards discovered that there was a defect in the appointment of any Board Member or that any of them were disqualified from holding office, or had vacated office, or were not entitled to vote, be as valid as if every such person had been duly appointed and was qualified and had continued to be a Board Member and had been entitled to vote.

A resolution in writing signed by all the Board Members entitled to receive notice of a meeting of the Board of Directors and to attend and vote at it shall be as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a meeting of the Board of Directors duly convened and held and may consist of several documents in the like form each signed by one or more Board Members.

The Board of Directors is from time to time empowered by subscription levy or otherwise to require a member or members to contribute such sums of money to the funds of the Company and/or the Competition as may be necessary for the proper conduct of the business of the Company. Such contributions by members may be collected by deducting such contributions from any sums due to members or by whatever other means the Board of Directors thinks fit. Such sums may also include the costs attributed to the Company to defend a challenge through the courts or by any other legal challenge by a Member Club that was unsuccessful. There shall be added to any sums to be contributed by members, if applicable, value added tax at the appropriate rate.
The Board Members shall not have any right to appoint any other person to be his alternate or to act on his behalf as a Board Member.

A Board Meeting may be convened by any Board Member in the case of urgent company business where it is impractical to convene a full Board Meeting because of time constraints, to be held by way of a conference call and the provision of Article 22.2 shall apply to the participants in the conference call. Notice of the Board Meeting shall be given by telephone or e-mail as soon as reasonably possible to all Board Members. Minutes of such a Board Meeting shall be circulated to all Board Members (Whether they shall have participated in the meeting or not) as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter and in any event not later than 14 days from the date of the meeting.

nodes.title: VOTES OF BOARD MEMBERS WITH AN INTEREST IN THE PROCEEDINGS

nodes.body: Save as otherwise provided by these Articles, a Board Member shall not vote at a meeting of the Board of Directors on any resolution concerning a matter in which he or any Club in which he is involved has, directly or indirectly, an interest or which is material and which conflicts or may conflict with the interests of the Company unless his interests or duty arises only because the case falls within one or more of the following paragraphs:
the resolution relates to the giving to him of a guarantee, security, or indemnity in respect of money lent to, or an obligation incurred by him for the benefit of the Company;

the resolution relates to the giving a third party of a guarantee, security or indemnity in respect of an obligation of the Company for which the Board Member has assumed responsibility in whole or part and whether alone or jointly with others under a guarantee or indemnity or by the giving of security;

his interest arises by virtue of his subscribing or agreeing to subscribe for any debentures of the Company or by virtue of his being, or intending to become, a participant in the underwriting or sub-underwriting of an offer of any debentures by the Company for subscriptions, purchase or exchange; or
the resolution relates in any way to a retirement benefits scheme which has been approved, or is conditional upon approval, by the Inland Revenue for taxation purposes.
A Board Member shall not be counted in the quorum present at a meeting in relation to a resolution on which he is not entitled to vote.

The Company may by ordinary resolution suspend or relax to any extent, either generally or in respect of any particular matter, any provision of the Articles prohibiting a Board Member from voting at a meeting of the Board of Directors or of a Board of the Board of Directors.

Where proposals are under consideration concerning the appointment of two or more Board Members to offices or employments with the Company or any body corporate in which the Company is interested the proposals may be divided and considered in relation to each Board Member separately and (provided he is not for another reason precluded from voting) each of the Board Members concerned shall be entitled to vote and be counted in the quorum in respect of each resolution except that concerning his own appointment.

If a question arises at a meeting of the Board of Directors or of a Board of the Board of Directors as to the right of a Board Member to vote, the question may, before the conclusion of the meeting, be referred to the chairman of the meeting and his ruling in relation to any Board Member other than himself shall be final and conclusive.

nodes.title: LIFE MEMBERS, PRESIDENT AND VICE-PRESIDENTS
nodes.body: The Board of Directors may elect and remove Life Members, a President and up to 3 Vice-Presidents for services to the Company, who need not be members of a Club. Any such appointment is honorary only and confers no powers on the appointee.
The activities of the Competition shall be administered by the Company in accordance with the Rules to which all Clubs shall adhere.

The Company shall have:(a) these Articles of Association ("Articles");(b) Standardised Rules governing the sporting and operational conduct of the Competitions issued by The Football Association ("League Rules"); and(c) Regulations and Directives issued by the Board pursuant to the League Rules.
Any amendment to these Articles shall require a Special Resolution of the Members.
Amendments to the League Rules, where there is an FA authority to amend, may be amended, added to or revoked by Ordinary Resolution of the Members.

The Board shall have power to issue Regulations and Operational Directives consistent with the League Rules for the proper administration of the Competitions, provided such Regulations shall not conflict with these Articles or any resolution of the Members.

For the avoidance of doubt, all football operational matters relating to the running of the Competitions shall be determined by Ordinary Resolution unless expressly stated otherwise in these Articles.

Notice of proposed amendments to the Articles or League Rules (other than those approved by the Board of Directors) to be considered at an annual general meeting shall be submitted in writing to the General Manager not later than 31 January prior to the relevant annual general meeting and must be proposed by a member and seconded by a second member.

Notice of the proposals for amendment of the Rules, together with any proposals by the Board of Directors shall be circulated with the notice of the Meeting at least twenty-one clear days before the date of the general meeting.

No amendment or addition to the Rules shall become operative until approved by the Football Association. Subject as aforesaid, Rules and decisions made in accordance therewith will be effective when notified to the members in writing.

nodes.title: MINUTES
nodes.body: The Board of Directors shall cause minutes to be made in books kept for the purpose:
of all appointments of officers made by the Board of Directors; and
of all proceedings at meetings of the Company, and of the Board of Directors, and of Boards of the Board of Directors, including the names of the persons present at each such meeting.

nodes.title: ACCOUNTS
nodes.body: No member shall (as such) have any right of inspecting any accounting records or other book or document of the Company except as conferred by statute or authorised by the Board of Directors or by the ordinary resolution of the Company.
Any notice to be given to or by any person pursuant to the Articles shall be in writing except that a notice calling a meeting of the Board of Directors need not be in writing.

The Company may give any notice to a member or other individual entitled to receive it either personally, electronically or by sending it by post in a prepaid envelope addressed to the member or individual at a nominated address or by leaving it at that address. A member or other individual whose nominated address is not within the United Kingdom and who gives to the Company an address within the United Kingdom at which notices may be given to him shall be entitled to have notices given to him at that address, but otherwise no such person shall be entitled to receive any notice from the Company.
A member present, either in person or by proxy, at any meeting of the Company shall be deemed to have received notice of the meeting and, where requisite, of the purposes for which it was called.

Proof that an envelope containing a notice was properly addressed, prepaid and posted shall be conclusive evidence that the notice was given. A notice shall be deemed to be given at the expiration of 24 hours after the envelope containing it was posted.

nodes.title: INDEMNITY
nodes.body: Subject to the provisions of the Act but without prejudice to any indemnity to which a Board Member may otherwise be entitled, every Board Member or auditor of the Company shall be indemnified out of the assets of the Company against any liability incurred by him in defending any proceedings, whether civil or criminal, in which judgment is given in his favour or in which he is acquitted or in connection with any application in which relief is granted to him by the court from liability for negligence, default, breach of duty or breach of trust relation to the affairs of the Company.

nodes.title: COMPETITION MEMBERS OF OTHER BODIES
nodes.body: The Company may by ordinary resolution passed at the annual general meeting or at any general meeting become a member of any inter competition board or combination of competitions in the United Kingdom or enter into any arrangement with any competition or combination of competitions and be subject to the rules and bye-laws of such boards or combinations and be bound by such agreements and, in like manner, may alter or terminate such membership or agreement.

The Board, without prejudice to its existing rights, powers and duties in connection with the management of the business of the Company and/or the Competition, shall have full authority at its discretion to negotiate and procure the Company and/or the Competition to enter into any Commercial Agreement and the Clubs shall comply with all obligations on their part which may be contained or referred to in any such Commercial Agreement.

All profits deriving from Commercial Agreements shall belong beneficially to those Clubs which are Members of the Competition throughout the season in which those profits are made in the ratio determined by the Board from time to time.
